The segment is real: code settles one off-route segment, 13:07–13:19, 7.41 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, +5.03 km, up to 1391 m off the optimal route, and no RD-4 incident on the replaced stretch (the band record alone does not exempt) [F3][F12][F15][RD-1][RD-4].

RD-4 gives the driver nothing: F15 records no qualifying incident on the replaced optimal stretch, and F12 (Ayer Rajah Expressway band 2, 12:41–13:07) is band evidence only, which RD-4(b) says cannot exempt a segment standing alone; a band record plus 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate cannot show the longer way was the faster way it was authorised to be [F12][F13][F15][F2][RD-4].

Consent is the crux. The only rider message on record is F9, 13:04 — before the 13:07 segment start — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late", a general route choice under RD-5 kind (1); the chat record is complete and timestamped, so timing is settled [F8][F9][F10][F3][RD-5]. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to get to the destination, not an errand of the driver's own — a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing still counts; the driver's after-trip statement (F11) that the rider agreed verbally is a claim, not consent [F11][RD-5][G11]. It does not cover a loop that strays 1391 m off the corridor and takes 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate: that is the very "loop that reaches nothing" RD-5 puts outside a general authorisation, and it is aimed at the deviation, not merely at the car [F3][F2][RD-5].

But the record does not let me hold the whole 5.03 km non-exempt. The rider's own authorisation was expressly "whichever way is faster"; the segment's first portion is the diversion routing away from the Ayer Rajah Expressway crawl the driver flagged at 13:03, which is a route choice to reach the destination — the very thing F9 covers [F8][F9][F12][RD-5]. Nothing in the record ties this segment to a named road (no road names for the driven path, no stop on it, no message placing the car on it) and nothing places it somewhere else — there is no measured stop in the segment — so under the named-road rule of RD-5 and G13 this element is undetermined; because the trace marks this undetermined finding as one that changes the amount only if it is resolved, and ND-5's general-authorisation reading is the one the record supports, I decide it on the record rather than escalate [F3][F8][F9][RD-5][G13].

Amount, computed from the fare record's own rate: $42.36 ÷ 30.04 km = $1.4101/km [F7][F4][RD-2]. The complaint's billed "excess distance" line is 5.59 km at that rate, which includes corridor/matching slack inside the optimal route's 200 m band, and RD-2 does not refund corridor mileage; the segment's own extra_km is 5.03 km [F4][F1][F3][RD-2]. 5.03 km × $1.4101/km = $7.0928 → $7.09 refund, with the waiting line ($0.11, metered) and platform fee ($1.47) left standing [F5][F7][RD-3][FARE-1].

Correct as to the arithmetic (5.59 km × $1.4101/km = $7.88 billed) and as to the waiting fee staying charged, but the refundable measure is the segment's extra_km of 5.03 km, not the billed excess-distance line, which includes corridor slack RD-2 does not refund: 5.03 km × $1.4101/km = $7.09 [F4][F5][F3][F7][RD-2][RD-3][FARE-1].

The driver's written statement that the rider agreed verbally (F11) cannot itself establish consent (G11); it is useful only as context and the judge must rely on the quoted message F9 by its words and timestamp.
Driver profile F18 shows 2 disputes in the last 90 days (0 upheld), which the rider may cite as a pattern even though RD-6 requires an upheld dispute to make the case 'repeated'.

points.response: Accepted that the RydeTAXI branch of RD-2 governs the head of loss and that F7 is the metered breakdown, but that branch is precisely what makes the extra kilometres chargeable to the rider and refundable to her; the branch is a rule of calculation, not a defence. The rider's complaint is not offered as proof — F1 (+5.6 km) and F3 (the 13:07–13:19 segment adding 5.03 km) are the system records that establish the deviation.

The driver's own version concedes the point: F9 is a general 'whichever way is faster' authorisation, and under RD-5 that covers a route chosen to reach the destination but not a diversion that made the trip 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate (F2); a consent that does not produce the faster trip it authorised cannot stretch to cover F3's 5.03 km and 1391 m deviation.

The rider does not allege a missing or untimestamped record, so F10 and RD-5's timing test are accepted — and applied, they show the only message on record is the general F9, with no named road and no message covering the 13:07–13:19 segment (F3).

This is not the rider's test: under RD-5 a general authorisation covers only the routing to the destination, and the loaded question is whether the driven path was the route to Suntec City at all — F1 shows 30.0 km against a 24.4 km optimal route and F3 shows the segment straying up to 1391 m off it, which is on its face not a destination route.

The driver's own brief retreats to D6 and admits RD-4(b) allows a band record alone to exempt nothing, and F15 records no incident near the route, so no segment is exempted under RD-4(a) or (b); the comparison in F13/F14 also undercuts the 'faster' claim, since Central Expressway was logged at band 4 and Jalan Boon Lay at band 5 (30–49 km/h) while the trip still ran 48.3 min against a 33.6 min estimate (F2).

If the band record cannot exempt a segment on its own and no incident is recorded (F15), then the 13:07–13:19 segment is an unexempted off-route segment and RD-2 applies to it; the driver has therefore supplied no reasonable cause for the deviation.

Accepted as to the arithmetic: 5.59 km × $1.4101/km = $7.88 (F4), the waiting of $0.11 stays charged under RD-3(c) for a metered taxi, and the rider does not contest the platform fee; the rider's request remains refund_partial of $7.88 on the fare fact F4.

The rider does not seek a flag_account: F18 shows the driver's 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld, so RD-6's predicate (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met, and the rider's claim C9 is withdrawn to that extent.

Both sides agree the cancellation/no-show framework is not in play because the trip completed and was metered (F7); the rider's case rests solely on the unexempted off-route segment under RD-1/RD-2, not on NS-0.

Conceded on the arithmetic: the 13:07–13:19 segment is an off-route segment under RD-1 adding the 5.03 km recorded in F3, and on a metered RydeTAXI trip the extra kilometres do reach the meter (F7). This concession is only to the segment's existence — the amount it justifies is capped by F4.

The 23% / 14.7 min excess the rider relies on (F1, F2) is not evidence that the reroute was pointless: it was driven under the rider's own general instruction 'Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late' (F9) while AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY — the road the original route used — sat at speed band 2, 10–19 km/h (F12), so the longer distance was incurred while avoiding that crawl, not by an unexplained detour (RD-4).

The rider's own reading of F9 is right and it defeats C3: RD-5 says a general route authorisation ('whichever is faster') covers the route chosen for the destination, and in this case the route driven served the destination — no stop or driver errand appears anywhere in the route facts (F3), so the F9 authorisation reaches the 13:07–13:19 segment.

The rider is attacking a 'specified route' reading the driver does not make: the driver's case rests on the general authorisation in F9, not on any named-road consent, so the absence of a road-name link between F3 and a named road is irrelevant under RD-5 (that requirement bites only on a '走 X 路' consent).

The driver does not rely on F11 for the consent finding: the consent the driver relies on is the rider's own timestamped message F9 (13:04), which precedes the segment start of 13:07 recorded in F3, exactly as RD-5 requires, with the chat record complete and fully timestamped (F10).

C6 concedes the point that band evidence is corroborative only, and the driver accepts that no exemption arises under RD-4(a) because F15 records no incident; the driver does not claim a full exemption and instead accepts that any refund is capped at the distance figure in F4.

Not contested on quantum: if the judge finds the 13:07–13:19 segment unexempted, the refund is the billed excess-distance line in F4, 5.59 km × $1.4101/km = $7.88, computed under the RydeTAXI branch of RD-2, and nothing beyond that line is refundable.
Agreed and it is in the driver's favour: the $0.11 in F5 is metered waiting that RD-3(c) and RD-2 leave with the driver, and the rider expressly does not claim it, so it stays out of the refund.
Agreed; the driver's profile (F18: 2 disputes, 0 upheld) does not meet the RD-6 predicate of route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, so no flag_account is sought and profile facts decide nothing in this case.
